belief: If I had done something different, they would still be alive.
origins: After a death, the mind searches for what could have been done: a symptom missed, a call not made, a different route, a different decision. This is a normal part of grief, because the alternative, that we could not control it, is frightening. But it can turn into heavy self-blame.
teaches: The psalmist says, “My times are in Your hands.” Scripture teaches that God alone numbers our days. “Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His saints.” David, after his child died, said, “Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.” The psalmist says, “Even if He causes grief, He will show compassion according to His abundant loving devotion.” We act on what we know at the time. Hindsight gives clarity that was not available then, and love does not make us all-knowing or all-powerful.
self_statements: If only I had called sooner.
errors: Judging past choices by what I know now.
Taking responsibility for something beyond my control.
Believing that the right action would have guaranteed a different outcome.
Insisting that I should have known.
questions: What did I know at the time, and what did I only learn afterward?
Could I realistically have prevented this?
What would I say to a friend who felt this way?
What did I do out of love?
What does it mean that God holds our times?
Is there something real I need to confess, and if so, what does God say about forgiveness?
truth: I acted with the knowledge and strength I had at the time. Hindsight shows me things I could not see then. My times, and theirs, are in God’s hands. I can grieve without condemning myself, and I can receive God’s compassion.
hw_truths: My times are in God’s hands.
I acted on what I knew.
Love does not give control over life and death.
I can be gentle with myself.
log: Each day, write one thing you did out of love for them.
actions: List the information and options you actually had.
Tell your loved one what you wish you could say.
Share the guilt with a pastor, counselor, or friend.
Say, “I did the best I could with what I knew.”
prayer: Lord, I keep asking what I could have done. You know my heart and You hold our days. Release me from self-blame, and help me trust that my times and theirs are in Your hands. Amen.
hw_questions: What did I do out of love?
What would I tell a friend?
What do I need to confess?
name_example: Sarah can write: “My times are in Your hands, and so are theirs.”
